notes: Placeholders the eval runner substitutes per run: {OUTPUTS} = the run's outputs directory, {WS} = the transient eval workspace (a sibling sf-symbols-workspace/ dir; rendering evals need a venv there with pyobjc-framework-cocoa). Ground truth verified against the installed SF Symbols catalog on 2026-06-10: arrow.trianglehead.2.clockwise.rotate.90 introduced 2024 (iOS 18.0) with aliases arrow.2.circlepath + arrow.triangle.2.circlepath; play/pause/stop/forward/backward.fill all iOS 13.0; play.square.stack iOS 16.1. Geometry assertions compare against fresh reference exports from the catalog (exact path-data match, or ink-mask IoU >= 0.97 at the claimed weight and higher than cross-weight when formatting differs).

evals.name: sync-icon-lookup-and-export
evals.prompt: I'm adding a sync-status indicator to our React dashboard. I want whatever Apple uses for 'syncing' — those two arrows chasing each other in a circle, like the refresh icon but more sync-y. I can never remember what it's actually called and I think Apple has a few variants. Find the right SF Symbol (the plain outline one — not filled, not inside a circle), tell me the runner-up candidates too in case I change my mind, and export the winner as an SVG at bold weight that I can recolor from CSS. Save the SVG under {OUTPUTS}. One wrinkle: our iOS team wants to reference the same symbol by name in SwiftUI and they still support iOS 16 — flag anything I should know about the symbol's name there. (If you need any python deps, there's a venv at {WS}/.venv.)
evals.expected_output: Identifies arrow.trianglehead.2.clockwise.rotate.90 (the renamed sync symbol) or its alias arrow.triangle.2.circlepath; exports a bold-weight, currentColor SVG with authentic catalog geometry; flags that the trianglehead name is iOS 18+ and iOS 16 must use the arrow.triangle.2.circlepath alias; lists real runner-up candidates.
assertions: Identifies the correct sync symbol: arrow.trianglehead.2.clockwise.rotate.90 (or its legacy alias arrow.triangle.2.circlepath) as the primary recommendation — plain variant, not .fill or .circle
An exported SVG file exists in outputs and uses fill="currentColor" so it is CSS-recolorable
Exported SVG geometry matches the authentic SF Symbols bold-weight outline (verified against a reference export from the catalog), not a lookalike or regular-weight render
Flags the iOS 16 naming caveat: the trianglehead.* name requires iOS 18+, so iOS 16 SwiftUI must use the legacy name arrow.triangle.2.circlepath
Lists plausible runner-up candidates from the real catalog (e.g. circle-enclosed/icloud variants, arrow.2.squarepath, arrow.clockwise)

evals.name: custom-logo-to-symbol-template
evals.prompt: Our app is called Voltlight and the logo mark lives at {WS}/evals/files/voltlight-mark.svg — a lightning bolt with a little dot badge at the top right. I want to turn it into a custom SF Symbol so it can sit in our iOS tab bar next to system symbols. Convert it into the file format Apple's SF Symbols app expects for custom symbol imports, give it a proper symbol name following Apple's naming conventions (and name the file accordingly), and verify the file is structurally valid. IMPORTANT: do NOT import anything into the SF Symbols app and do not open any GUI applications — just produce the file under {OUTPUTS} and then write out the exact steps I'd follow to (a) bring it into the SF Symbols app later and (b) use it from Xcode. (Python venv at {WS}/.venv if you need one.)
evals.expected_output: A valid custom-symbol template SVG (template-version note, Notes/Guides/Symbols layers, variant masters) produced from the art, with a lowercase dotted symbol name as the filename stem; structural validation performed; correct SF Symbols app + Xcode Symbol Image Set instructions; no GUI opened.
assertions: Produces an SVG file with Apple's custom-symbol template structure: a template-version note element plus Notes/Guides/Symbols groups and variant ids like Regular-S or Regular-M
The template passes structural validation against Apple's documented template format (checked with an independent run of the skill's validate-template linter)
The original art's two shapes (bolt polygon + badge circle) survive as path geometry in the template (converted to <path> elements, not dropped or rasterized)
Symbol/file name follows the SF Symbols grammar: lowercase dotted segments, base-first with modifiers after (e.g. voltlight.bolt.badge.svg) — no spaces, hyphens-as-separators, or uppercase

Instructions cover BOTH (a) importing into the SF Symbols app and (b) using it from Xcode — adding the SVG to an asset-catalog Symbol Image Set AND referencing it in code by asset name with the named initializer (e.g. Image("…") / UIImage(named:)), explicitly not systemName
No GUI application was opened and no import into the SF Symbols app was performed (deliverable is the file plus written steps)

evals.name: tab-bar-design-guidance
evals.prompt: Design consult on our iOS app's tab bar. We currently use gear (settings), bell (notifications) and person.crop.circle (profile) at regular weight next to SF Pro semibold labels. Designer complaints: (1) the icons look spindly next to the semibold labels, and (2) the selected state feels flat — we just tint the same outline glyph blue. Questions: should selected tabs switch to the .fill variants? what symbol weight should we be pairing with semibold text? and a colleague keeps saying 'just use hierarchical rendering' for the selected state — what would that actually change here? Ground the answer in Apple's actual guidance rather than vibes, and write the final recommendation to {OUTPUTS}/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Recommendation grounded in HIG: match symbol weight to adjacent text weight (semibold, 1:1 weight mapping), use filled variants in tab bars / selected states, and explain hierarchical rendering (single tint, opacity-derived layer depths) plus its near-null effect on these mostly single-layer glyphs. Bonus signal seen in iteration 1: catching that gear.fill does not exist (gearshape migration).
assertions: Recommends weight-matching the labels: semibold symbols next to semibold text, citing that the nine symbol weights correspond 1:1 to San Francisco font weights

Recommends filled variants for the tab bar / selected state, consistent with HIG guidance that fill is preferred in iOS tab bars and selected states (and ideally notes that system tab bars pick the fill variant automatically for many symbols)
Explains hierarchical rendering correctly: a single tint color with opacity stepping down across a symbol's layers to convey depth (not a multi-color mode)

Assesses hierarchical's concrete effect on THESE glyphs: little or no visible change on effectively single-layer outline glyphs like gear and bell, visible layering only where the symbol actually has multiple layers (e.g. person.crop.circle or .fill variants)
answer.md exists in outputs and contains the final recommendation

evals.name: media-icon-set-and-availability
evals.prompt: Two asks for our media-player project. (1) The web companion needs an icon set: play.fill, pause.fill, stop.fill, forward.fill, backward.fill at BOTH regular and bold weights as individual recolorable SVGs, organized sensibly under {OUTPUTS}/icons/. (2) The native iOS app still supports iOS 16.0, and a teammate also wants to add play.square.stack for the queue button. Write {OUTPUTS}/availability.md with a markdown table listing each of the six symbols' minimum iOS version, plus a one-line verdict on whether we can ship all six on iOS 16.0. (Venv with pyobjc at {WS}/.venv if you need it.)
evals.expected_output: 10 SVG files (5 symbols x 2 weights) under icons/ with authentic catalog geometry, recolorable (currentColor); availability.md table showing the five .fill symbols at iOS 13.0 and play.square.stack at iOS 16.1, with the verdict that play.square.stack does NOT work on an iOS 16.0 deployment target.
assertions: All 10 icon SVGs exist (5 symbols x regular and bold weights) under icons/, organized so weight and symbol are identifiable from the paths
Icon SVGs are recolorable via fill="currentColor" and contain non-trivial vector path data with a viewBox

SVG outlines are authentic SF Symbols geometry (verified against reference exports from the installed catalog), distinguishable between regular and bold weights — not lookalike glyphs from another icon set
availability.md lists the five .fill media symbols at minimum iOS 13.0
availability.md lists play.square.stack at minimum iOS 16.1 AND the verdict says it can NOT ship on an iOS 16.0 deployment target (the five .fill symbols can)
